title: Eight Ways to Reach a Pose: Closed Form Inverse Kinematics for an Arm With a Spherical Wrist, and the Arms It Does Not Work For

questions.question: Why does a spherical wrist make inverse kinematics easy?
options: Its three joints can be solved by a table
It removes the elbow from the problem
The point where the last three axes meet is fixed by the first three joints alone
It makes every pose have one solution
questions.explanation: The wrist centre does not move when the wrist turns. So the first three joints are found from its position, and the last three from the orientation that is left.

questions.question: How many solutions did the solver give on average for a reachable pose?
questions.explanation: The arm can face the point or reach back over its shoulder, with the elbow up or down, and the wrist one way or flipped: two times two times two.

questions.question: A pose 1.5 m from the base gave how many solutions?
options: 8, all at the limit of reach
1, the nearest reachable pose
4, with the elbow straight
0: out of reach, an empty list
questions.explanation: The arm is not that long. An empty list is the honest answer; the 4 was at the very edge of reach, where elbow up and down coincide.

questions.question: Is the UR5's wrist spherical (1) or not (0)?
options: 1: its last three axes meet
0: its fifth joint is offset
1, when the fifth joint is at zero
It depends on the tool offset
questions.explanation: The table's d5 is 0.09465 m, so the last three axes do not meet at a point and the split into position and orientation does not apply.

questions.question: What is the test that matters for an inverse kinematics solver?
options: That every solution put through forward kinematics reaches the pose
That it gives eight answers every time
That it gives back the angles the pose was made from
That its answers are within the joint limits
questions.explanation: Several sets of angles reach one pose, so matching the starting angles proves little. Every answer put back through forward kinematics reached the pose.

questions.question: Which of the eight does the solver pick?
options: The one with the elbow up
The one with the smallest joint angles
None: it gives all, and the caller picks within the limits, nearest the present angles
The one nearest the zero pose
questions.explanation: All eight are correct. With limits of 120 degrees only 1 of the 8 was allowed, and which of the allowed ones to take depends on where the arm is now.
